text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition agree to extend the monopoly of national post office Deutsche Post AG from January 1, 1998 for five years to the end of 2002, but only for letters weighing under 100 grams (3.5 ounces).

- Bavarian sister party of Kohl's Christian Democrats the Christian Social Union (CSU) says does not expect any concrete results from planned tax reform talks between the ruling coalition and the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), but sees a working group being set up.
- Ruling coalition unexpectedly postpones decision over health reform.
- German index of 30 leading shares pushes to new record high of 3,276.16 spurred by climbing dollar and German Bunds.
- The number of self-employed in Germany climbs to 590,000 in 1996, up 5.5 percent.
HANDELSBLATT
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel says new budget austerity measures cannot be ruled out.
- Dollar movement erratic, first climbing to three-year high of 1.7050 marks and then falling back to 1.6850.
- New chairman Klaus Lederer at embattled German plant engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG plans massive job cuts under a restructuring aimed at wiping out losses.
- Coalition postpones health reforms.
- Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest bank, reports sharply higher-than-expected operating profit after risk provisions which jumped 37 percent to 5.8 billion marks.
- German post office keeps monopoly on letters weighing up to 100 grams until the end of 2002.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer and junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) want employees to pay for future increases in health insurance contributions.

- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber criticises Prague government for attempt to reinterpret reconcilliation agreement between two countries to avoid a full apology for the post-war expulsion of so-called Sudenten Germans.
- Around 11 percent of the German economy's earnings goes to health costs.
- Dollar rises above 1.70 mark level.
- Post office holds onto monopoly on letters weighing under 100 grams until end of 2002.
DIE WELT
- Coalition considering further austerity measures, but decision to come only after tax reform talks with SPD next Monday.
- Post office keeps limited monopoly until 2002.
- Jordan's King Hussein says the U.S. and European Union states must encourage Israel to lessen pressure on the Palestinians.
- Health reform decision postponed.
- Birth rate climbs by 11.5 percent in east Germany. The birth rate for the whole of Germany climbs for the first time since unification.
